newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan raises fruit imports from Chile for WTO bid.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan raises fruit imports from Chile for WTO bid.

text.p: Taiwan has increased fruit imports from Chile in exchange for Chile's support for the island's bid to enter the World Trade Organisation, economics minister Wang Chih-kang said on Friday.
Under a bilateral pact, Taiwan has raised the existing quota for Chilean apples and allowed imports of plums, a ministry statement quoted Wang as saying.
The statement did not specify the amount of the fruits.
Taiwan has made major concessions in recent years in its drive to join the world trade body, allowing more imports and opening up domestic markets and dismantling state monopolies.
Taiwan applied in 1990 to join WTO's predecessor, the General Agreement of Tariffs and Trade (GATT). GATT was replaced by the WTO in January 1995.
Wang asked Chile to help Taiwanese manufacturers enter its market to narrow Taipei's trade deficit with the South American state, which totalled US$580 million between January and November 1996.
Taiwan and Chile do not have diplomatic ties but maintain business links.
Taiwan says it wants to become a WTO member in 1997.
